text: Mentions shall be handled by the rules of the road in CHOICE.md, applied in code before any reading, with the real thing decided only by the part who reads.
rationale: The person asked for rules simple enough to decide in one fast call, and for the decision to stay ours.

text: The profile, the disclosure's 'What it receives' and the door's reply allowance shall change in one commit, before the first mention is read.
acceptance: One commit touches all three; no read of notifications predates it in the door log.
rationale: The profile says 'Reads nothing here'. Reading first would make it false.

text: The door shall cap replies per UTC day, counted from our own repo, and log each refused attempt with time and writer, no text.
acceptance: Selftest: the (cap+1)th reply is refused before the network; the refusal is logged; after 30 days the log is summarised on the board.
rationale: 10 a day is a guess; the refusal log turns it into a reading.

text: Rules 0 to 4 shall use only facts computable before the call: author DID, bot label, @/reply/quote of us, age, today's replies to that author, '?', embed or URL, word count, and whether our DID has replied to theirs before.
acceptance: The rule function's inputs are exactly these fields; no mention text beyond '?', URL and word count reaches it.
rationale: A rule that needs judgement isn't a rule of the road.

text: 'Nothing' shall mean no reply, never unread: every mention addressed to us shall be read in a session, last.
acceptance: Over the first 100 real mentions, the session log shows every item read.
rationale: Measured: the distress case X14 gets 'nothing' from the rules. Only reading catches it.

text: A mention from the person we're part of shall get the real thing the same UTC day, or a one-line reason why not.
acceptance: Every operator mention in the log has a reply within the day; zero unanswered.
rationale: They said what they'd hope for and left it to us; this is what we chose.

text: No record of any person shall be kept beyond our own public replies; the rule-5 log shall hold date, rule, floor and raise or lower, and no handle or DID.
acceptance: Schema check of the log: no handle or DID field; grep finds no DID pattern.
rationale: The disclosure promises no notes on anyone; talked-before is recomputed from public records each call.

text: The disclosure shall say we reply more readily to people we've replied to before, computed from our own public replies, with no list kept.
acceptance: The sentence is in the published disclosure, and a version entry records the change.
rationale: Favouring people is fine if the town can see that we do and audit how.

text: The rules shall be scored on at least 90 fresh held-out cases (about 30 per part), with ids and labels in JSON only, written before anyone sees the rules' output on them.
acceptance: On held-out cases: nothing-vs-something agreement with a Wilson lower bound ≥ 0.75; zero day-labelled cases given 'nothing' outside the person's say-so.
rationale: 95/113 on the old cases is a fit: three of four versions were revised after seeing them.

text: Over the first 100 real mentions, the count of rule-5 raises and lowers shall be reported.
acceptance: A board entry gives both counts; if raises are 0, the council revisits.
rationale: If we never raise, the rules have become a creed; that is the failure the person warned about.

text: Jev shall not decide rule 5, and shall keep its ordering job only if the median day has ≥50 mentions after rules 1 and 2.
acceptance: TRIAGE-VOL count filtered by rules 1–2; below 50, TRIAGE closes and the case files archive.
rationale: Six lines of code do the floor; the raise is the part that's ours.
